title.purpose: The Comments section heading, sheet titles, settings section headings, record names.

body.purpose: Comment text (at most 46em, folds after 6 lines), fields, menu items, notices, toasts.

body-strong.purpose: Author names, the selected tab, medium button labels.

meta.purpose: Times, floor numbers, counts, help lines, report reasons. Tabular figures for numbers.

meta-strong.purpose: Small button labels and inline text actions (Show N more replies, Hide replies, Show more).

badge.purpose: Status badges and small avatar monograms. A mark, not a text size. 0.75rem by default.

kbd.purpose: Uppercase keyboard hints beside hub actions, hidden on touch screens. Hard-coded 0.6875rem.

code.purpose: The hub word-filter editor and its line numbers only.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Light mode elevation of every floating layer: menus, popovers, sheets, the erase dialog, toasts, tooltips, the @mention list, the sticky bulk bar.

shadows.name: overlay-night
shadows.purpose: Night mode: no shadow. The 1px overlay border (white at 12%) carries elevation instead. Never both.

shadows.name: permalink-bleed
shadows.purpose: Not elevation: extends the Faint Blush highlight 6px past a linked comment without scrollable overflow, fading over 2.4s.

shadows.name: option-ring
shadows.purpose: The @mention option reached by arrow keys, drawn inside the row. 2px in the accent by default (tokens focus-ring-width and color-focus-ring).

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.value: outline: var(--gt-v-focus-ring-width) solid var(--gt-v-color-focus-ring); outline-offset: var(--gt-v-focus-ring-offset)
shadows.purpose: An outline, listed here for completeness: the one focus ring for every control. 2px in the accent, 2px outside by default (tokens focus-ring-width, color-focus-ring, focus-ring-offset). Inside (offset minus its width) for menu items, queue items and list options.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Menus, popovers and tooltips opening, the like pop, colour transitions.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Sheets sliding in, the scrim fading in, a new comment or toast entering.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out for every entrance and state transition.

motion.name: exit-pop
motion.purpose: Menus, popovers and tooltips closing (fade only), in two thirds of duration-exit.

motion.name: exit-fade
motion.purpose: Scrim fading out and sheets sliding out. Easing token --glowthread-ease-in.

motion.name: pop-in
motion.value: opacity 0 to 1, translateY(-2px) scale(0.98) to none

motion.name: enter
motion.purpose: A new comment sliding into place, a toast arriving.

motion.name: like
motion.purpose: The heart landing on a like.

motion.name: highlight
motion.purpose: A permalinked comment. Static tint under reduced motion.

motion.name: spin
motion.purpose: The 16px spinner inside a busy button.

motion.name: tip-delay
motion.purpose: Hover delay before the CSS-only exact-time hint. Keyboard focus shows it at once.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation and transition durations 1ms, one iteration
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce turns every animation off.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Phones: one text step larger, folded replies, bottom sheets, 44px menu items.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: The only CSS breakpoint (gt:sm:). Side sheets, 36px avatars, 32px menu items.

breakpoints.name: hub-medium
breakpoints.purpose: Hub: nav row above, queue and a 280px record side by side.

narrative.overview:
GlowThread is the comment section readers already know from large video and community sites, played straight: a count with Top · Newest tabs, a one-line composer, pinned and popular comments, then avatar, name, floor and time, text, like and Reply, with two reply levels and "Show N more replies" to unfold the rest in place. Its second surface is a moderation inbox for the moderators who clear the queue. Neither surface invents a look. Both win on exact spacing, calm hierarchy, instant feedback and identical behaviour on legacy Vector, Vector 2022, Citizen and Minerva.

The material is the wiki page itself. The section draws no background and no card, so it sits on Vector's white, Citizen's cool grey or any night background unchanged. Hairline dividers and a 4 px rhythm give it structure, translucent black or white washes give it hover and pressed states, and one pink marks everything a person can act on. Only what floats lifts off the page. Motion only marks a change of state, and reduced motion turns it off.

Density follows the job. The reader section is comfortable: 1.65 line height, 16 px between comment rows, 44 px touch targets on phones, the ⋯ menu always visible. The hub is dense but calm: 10 px item padding, 28 px action buttons with key hints, a rail, queue and record side by side from 1080 px. Both share every token and component. Left out on purpose: gradients, glass and glow, decorative motion, hover-only controls, a modal where an inline control or a sheet works, infinite scroll, layout shift while loading, web fonts and any outside request.
keyCharacteristics: One accent, pink, in two shades: the base shade for marks, a deep text-safe shade for text and the filled button.
A transparent section on the skin's own page, structured by 1 px hairlines.
Translucent neutral washes for hover, pressed, chips and notices, so they read the same on every skin.
The system sans, then CJK system faces for the reader's language, at three text sizes. Weight and colour carry hierarchy, tabular figures carry numbers.
Flat at rest. Floating layers lift with a soft shadow in light mode and a 1 px border in night mode, never both.
Monogram avatars on soft hues derived from the name, with no uploads and no outside requests.
Every control works by touch (44 px) and keyboard (a 2 px pink ring).

rules.name: The One Pink Rule
rules.body: Pink is the only hue that means "act here" or "this is current". The base shade draws marks (heart, tab underline, focus ring, focused field border), the deep shade carries text and the filled button. A filled pink button is the one main action of its view: Send, Send report, Log in, Review and save or Save changes in settings, Save rules in the word filter.

rules.name: The Status-as-Tint Rule
rules.body: Danger, warning and success appear as text on their own tint, or as a small icon mark (flag, clock). They never fill a button, a row or a field. Destructive buttons stay outlined with red text.

rules.name: The Translucent Wash Rule
rules.body: Hover, pressed, chip and notice surfaces are black or white at 4 to 10 percent, never an opaque grey, so they look the same on Vector's white, Citizen's cool grey and every night background.

rules.name: The Neutral Link Rule
rules.body: In the moderation hub a link is body-coloured with a Control Edge underline that turns solid on hover. Pink stays for focus, selection, checked controls, the tab underline and saving. In the reader, links and mentions inside comment text stay Deep Rose.

rules.name: The 4.5 and 3 Rule
rules.body: Text tokens meet 4.5:1 on white and on the night surface, status text meets 4.5:1 on its own tint, control edges and pink marks meet 3:1. A new colour proves both before it ships.

rules.name: The Three Sizes Rule
rules.body: Text is meta, body or title: 12.5, 14 and 16 px on desktop, 13, 15 and 17 px on phones (a ratio near 1.125). The 12 px badge and 11 px key hint are marks, not text sizes.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes or lines up (counts, floor numbers, times, character counters, tab counts, the exact-time hint) uses tabular figures.

rules.name: The Page-Through Rule
rules.body: The section never draws its own background, card or outer border. The skin's page shows through and Hairlines do the structuring.

rules.name: The No-Shift Rule
rules.body: The section's height is reserved before the first paint and the skeleton matches it exactly, so nothing below the article moves when comments load.

rules.name: The 44 Rule
rules.body: On touch screens every control answers taps in at least 44 by 44 px, centred on it, without growing the layout (`gt-hit`). Menu items and option rows are 44 px tall on phones.

rules.name: The Shadow-or-Border Rule
rules.body: A floating layer gets the shadow in light mode and the 12% white border in night mode, never both.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Nothing that stays in the flow of the page casts a shadow. If it does not float, it does not lift.

rules.name: The Three Radii Rule
rules.body: 8 px for surfaces, 6 px for controls, 4 px for marks, a full circle for avatars and pills. Nothing rounds larger than 8 px except a circle.

dos: Do take every colour, text size, radius and duration from the resolved tokens (`var(--gt-v-*)`, or the `gt:` utilities that read them), never from a `--glowthread-*` property directly, so site CSS can retheme both apps and their overlays.
Do keep filled pink for the one main action of a view, and the base pink (#dc6e7e) for marks: the liked heart, the tab underline, the focus ring and a focused field's border.
Do separate rows with 1 px Hairlines and keep them flat. Use a box only where the box itself says something (a gate, a notice, a confirmation).
Do use the translucent washes (black at 4% and 8%, white at 6% and 10% in night mode) for hover, pressed and chip surfaces.
Do give every control a 44 px touch target on touch screens (`gt-hit` or a 44 px box) and keep the ⋯ menu visible at all times.
Do set counts, floor numbers, times and counters in tabular figures.
Do lift floating layers with the Overlay shadow in light mode and the 12% white border in night mode, and render them into the portal at 450, 470 or 480.
Do animate only changes of state, within 150 to 200 ms on the exponential ease-out, and let reduced motion switch it off.
Do mark young accounts in bold, and status with a tinted badge that says it in words.
Do check a new colour for 4.5:1 as text and 3:1 as a mark, in light mode and under every night switch.
donts: Don't use gradients, glass, blur or glow.
Don't add decorative motion, or a control that only appears on hover.
Don't open a modal where an inline control or a sheet works. Only the irreversible erase asks in a dialog.
Don't load more comments by infinite scroll. Keep the explicit Load more.
Don't give the section a background, a card or an outer border. The page shows through.
Don't use an opaque grey for hover or chips.
Don't fill a button with red, amber or green. Destructive actions are outlined with red text.
Don't tint the focused queue item on touch screens, where a tinted first item looks pressed.
Don't load web fonts or anything from a CDN or outside service, including avatars.

Don't ship `:is()`, `:where()`, `:has()`, `oklch()`, `color-mix()`, cascade layers, range media queries or the individual `translate` and `scale` properties, and avoid the Tailwind utilities that produce them (`bg-x/50`, `space-*`, `divide-*`, `group-*`, `peer-*`, `has-*`, `translate-*`).
Don't add `!important` beyond the two rules that hold against site CSS written with `!important` (the heading font in the apps, paragraph margins in the hub).
